question:
The numbers, in order, of each row and the numbers, in order, of each column of a \(5 \times 5\) array of integers form an arithmetic progression of length \(5.\) The numbers in positions \((5, 5),\) \((2, 4),\) \((4, 3),\) and \((3, 1)\) are \(0,\) \(48,\) \(16,\) and \(12,\) respectively. What number is in position \((1, 2)?\)

\[\begin{bmatrix} \cdot & ? & \cdot & \cdot & \cdot \\ \cdot & \cdot & \cdot & 48 & \cdot \\ 12 & \cdot & \cdot & \cdot & \cdot \\ \cdot & \cdot & 16 & \cdot & \cdot \\ \cdot & \cdot & \cdot & \cdot & 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
solution:
The zero in the bottom-right corner lets us describe the entire bottom row using just one unknown. Let \(a_{ij}\) denote the entry in row \(i\), column \(j\), and set \(a_{54}=d\). Because row \(5\) is arithmetic and ends in \(d,0\), it is
\[
4d,\ 3d,\ 2d,\ d,\ 0.
\]

In column \(1\), the entry in row \(4\) is the average of the entries in rows \(3\) and \(5\). Thus
\[
a_{41}=\frac{12+4d}{2}=6+2d.
\]
In column \(4\), there are three equal steps from \(a_{24}=48\) to \(a_{54}=d\). Row \(4\) is two of those steps below row \(2\), so
\[
a_{44}=48+\frac23(d-48)=16+\frac23d.
\]

Now use row \(4\). Column \(3\) is two of the three equal steps from column \(1\) to column \(4\), giving
\[
a_{43}=\frac{a_{41}+2a_{44}}3.
\]
Since \(a_{43}=16\),
\[
16=\frac{6+2d+2\left(16+\frac23d\right)}3.
\]
Multiplying by \(3\) and simplifying yields
\[
48=38+\frac{10}{3}d,
\qquad d=3.
\]

Therefore \(a_{53}=2d=6\). Moving upward in column \(3\), each step adds \(16-6=10\), so
\[
a_{13}=16+3\cdot10=46.
\]
Also, \(a_{51}=4d=12=a_{31}\). These entries are two steps apart in an arithmetic progression, so column \(1\) has common difference zero and \(a_{11}=12\).

Finally, the requested entry is the arithmetic mean of its neighbors in row \(1\):
\[
a_{12}=\frac{a_{11}+a_{13}}2=\frac{12+46}{2}=\boxed{29}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
